summary: Sweet acacia is a thorny shrub or small tree in the legume family with a pantropical distribution, though its exact native range remains disputed. It can remain evergreen or shed its leaves depending on location, thrives in dry, saline or sodium-rich soils, and readily resprouts after disturbance. Its fragrant flowers supply cassie perfume, while its pods feed wildlife and livestock; cattle also disperse the seeds and can help it spread through grazed land.

Madras thorn is a drought-resistant tree in the pea family, native to the Pacific coast and nearby highlands of Mexico, Central America and northern South America. Its ripe pink pods open to reveal seeds surrounded by sweet edible pulp, which attracts birds that disperse the seeds. Introduced widely beyond its native range, it has naturalized in places including the Caribbean, Florida, the Philippines and Guam, and is considered invasive in Hawaii.

summary: Black cherry is a deciduous New World tree or shrub widespread in North and Central America. It often acts as a pioneer in sunny old fields and forest edges, while its small reddish-black fruits feed birds and its foliage supports the caterpillars of hundreds of butterfly and moth species. The plant stores cyanide-forming compounds as a defence: crushed seeds can release hydrogen cyanide, and wilted leaves can poison livestock.

summary: Common houseleek is an evergreen succulent perennial native to the mountains of southern Europe. It forms compact rosettes and spreads through offsets, producing tall clusters of reddish-purple flowers in summer. For centuries it has also been planted on roofs: Roman-era and later European traditions held that it protected buildings from lightning, storms, fire or other harm, an association reflected in names linked to the thunder gods Jupiter and Thor.

Japanese superb fig is a tree native from Japan and China through parts of Southeast Asia to the Moluccas. It can grow from the ground or begin life on another tree, and may briefly lose its leaves in some regions. Its branch-borne figs are pollinated by a specialised fig wasp. In Taiwan, ants occupy cavities in young branches, feeding mainly on non-pollinating wasps and tending aphids and scale insects.

Allspice is a tree in the myrtle family native to Central America and the Caribbean. Male and female flowers grow on separate plants, a feature reflected in the name dioica. Its dried fruits are used as a spice whose aroma recalls cinnamon, black pepper and nutmeg, while processed seeds flavour preserves, meat and seafood. The tree also supplies aromatic materials for cosmetics and perfume, and its flowers are useful for honey production.

summary: Corn mint is a herbaceous perennial native across temperate parts of Europe, western and central Asia, eastern Siberia and North America. It favours moist ground, especially beside streams, and spreads from a creeping rootstock into upright or partly sprawling square stems. Pale purple flowers form in whorls at the leaf bases. Its leaves are eaten raw and have also been brewed as tea in traditional use.

details.scope: traditional use for colds or digestion

summary: Pointed boobialla is a shrub or small tree endemic to eastern Australia, where it grows in coastal rainforest and wet eucalyptus forest and is sometimes associated with mangroves. It bears sweet-scented white flowers marked with rows of purple spots, followed by dark blue or purple fruits. Its leaves contain visible oil dots, and the plant tolerates salt spray in cultivation, fitting its coastal distribution.

Glaucous glasswort is a salt-loving subshrub native to coastal areas around the Mediterranean and Red seas and parts of the Middle East. Its woody horizontal stems can root at their joints, while upright green stems are succulent and jointed. Experiments found that its seeds can germinate under very high salinity and that the plant accumulates sodium and chloride; it can also tolerate and accumulate cadmium in contaminated soil.

Pseudopediastrum boryanum is a microscopic green alga found in fresh waters worldwide, especially nutrient-rich waters. Its cells form flat, star-like colonies of four to 64 cells. It usually reproduces asexually when swimming spores form inside a parent cell and assemble into a new colony; sexual reproduction is rare. Its decay-resistant cell walls persist in lake sediments, although the organism is too widespread and taxonomically complex to be a precise ecological indicator.

Mountain pansy is a compact evergreen perennial found across Europe from the British Isles to the Balkans. Its flowers are usually golden yellow, though some plants produce blue, purple or blotched blooms. Two narrowly distributed forms in Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany have evolved on zinc or lead mine waste and can dominate these highly localised, metal-polluted habitats.

Biting stonecrop is a low evergreen perennial native to Europe, northern and western Asia, and North Africa. It forms dense mats on thin, dry ground where taller, faster-growing plants struggle, including shingle, walls, rocks and sandy coastal sites. Bright yellow star-shaped flowers rise above its fleshy leaves in summer. The leaves contain an acrid fluid that can cause skin rashes, and consumption of the plant is discouraged because it is considered poisonous.

details.effect: acrid fluid can cause skin rashes

summary: Small-flowered catchfly is an annual flowering plant native to Eurasia and North Africa and now widespread through much of the temperate world as a roadside weed. Its branching stems carry both long curling hairs and shorter glandular hairs. White, pink or two-coloured flowers develop in a terminal cluster, each enclosed by a hairy, ten-veined tube of fused sepals that inflates as the fruit forms.

Blackstonia acuminata is a flowering plant in the gentian family. The supplied account records two subspecies, B. acuminata subsp. acuminata and B. acuminata subsp. aestiva, as present and native in mainland Portugal. Neither subspecies is listed there as protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

Bearberry cotoneaster is a low evergreen shrub native to central and southern China and naturalised in Europe. Its creeping branches root wherever their nodes touch the ground, helping it spread into a broad cover. Fragrant white flowers with pink outer surfaces appear in late spring, followed by bright red fruits that remain well into winter. In its native mountain habitat it grows on cliffs and in open mixed forest on dry, lime-rich soils.

Dalmatian bellflower is a low evergreen perennial native to Croatia's Dalmatian Mountains. It forms broad mats that can be covered by deep purple or blue flowers from mid- to late summer. Beetles, flies, bees and butterflies may pollinate the flowers, which can also self-pollinate. As an alpine plant it needs free drainage and, in suitable conditions, rapidly colonises cracks and crevices in walls and paving.

Many-stalked spike-rush is a flowering plant in the sedge family. The supplied account records it from both mainland Portugal and the Azores and describes it as native to each of those regions. It is not listed as protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

Bufonia macropetala is a flowering plant in the pink family, Caryophyllaceae. The supplied account records its subspecies B. macropetala subsp. willkommiana as present and native in mainland Portugal. That subspecies is not listed there as protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

Woodland cudweed is a perennial in the daisy family, widespread across temperate parts of North America and Eurasia. Short runners spread beneath a stem that can range from low-growing to knee-high. Its pointed leaves are hairless above but woolly beneath, and become shorter and narrower towards the top. Small flower heads with pale brown florets appear from July to September, followed by hairy fruits with reddish bristles.

Martius' fan palm is a palm tree known from two distinct high-elevation populations in the Khasi Hills of north-eastern India and central northern Nepal, with further populations reported elsewhere in the region. It is recognised by evenly split fan leaves, coffee-bean-shaped seeds and a bare rather than fibrous trunk. Its leaves are used to make the Jhapi, a traditional Assamese head covering also used when honouring guests.

Pennsylvania cudweed is an annual flowering plant native to South America and introduced across Eurasia, Africa, Australia and North America. Its name is misleading because it is not native to Pennsylvania and is only marginally naturalised there. Woolly hairs give the leaves a light green appearance, while elongated clusters carry numerous small heads, each with a few purple disc flowers and no petal-like ray flowers.

Salacia chinensis is a climbing shrub in the bittersweet family, found widely across Southeast Asia and Australasia. It is also known as Chinese salacia, lolly berry and saptachakra. The plant has smooth leaves that vary from narrowly egg-shaped to elliptic, small yellow or yellow-green flowers with five petals, and fruits containing a single seed.

Lotus carpetanus is a mat-forming perennial native to the Iberian Peninsula. It has hairy leaves divided into three rounded lobes and pea-like flowers marked with orange streaks, with reddish hairs beneath the flower head. The species may be threatened, but the cited assessment describes confidence in that conclusion as low.

Philodendron campii is a flowering plant in the arum family, native to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru and adjoining parts of Brazil. It grows in wet tropical forests and is also offered commercially as a houseplant.
